units.title: Film ve kitap yorumu
units.description: Bir film ya da kitap hakkında gerekçeli yorumları okumak, dinlemek ve yazmak
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Bir film ya da kitap hakkındaki görüşünü gerekçeleriyle yazabilirsin.
- Aynı eser hakkındaki iki yorumu karşılaştırıp yazarların tutumunu ayırt edebilirsin.
- Bir kitap kulübü sohbetinde kimin neyi beğenip neyi beğenmediğini anlayabilirsin.
- Bir filmi bir dakikada anlatıp tavsiye edebilirsin.

## Strateji
- Yorum okurken önce puana ve son cümleye bak: yazarın genel tutumu çoğu zaman oradadır.
- **However, although, despite** gördüğünde dur: görüş tam orada döner.
- Gölgeleme (shadow) yaparken cümleyi bir kez dinle, sonra konuşmacıyla aynı anda, aynı vurguyla söyle. *I'd*, *kind of* gibi zayıf biçimleri yutmaya çalış.
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle. Soruları cevapla, sonra metni açıp kaçırdığın yerleri bul.
- Yorum yazarken üç paragraf kullan: özet, görüş ve gerekçe, puan ve tavsiye.

## Model metin
> Last month I read The Blue Door, a novel by a young writer from Sinop. It tells the story of a girl whose father has kept a lighthouse on a small island for thirty years. After her mother dies, she finds a box of letters that her mother had hidden. These letters explain why her father never left the island.
>
> In my opinion, the best thing about the book is the writing. The sea is described so well that you can almost hear it. However, the first hundred pages are quite slow, and I nearly gave up. The ending, which is open, may also disappoint some readers. Personally, I liked it because it lets you decide for yourself.
>
> Overall, I would give The Blue Door four stars. Although it starts slowly, it is a moving story about family and secrets. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys quiet, thoughtful books.

Yapı: 1. paragraf eseri tanıtır ve konuyu özetler (past perfect: *had hidden*). 2. paragraf bir artı ve bir eksiyi gerekçesiyle verir (*so … that*, *however*, *which*). 3. paragraf puan verir ve kime uygun olduğunu söyler (*although*, *who*).

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ Despite of the slow start, I liked it. ✅ **Despite** the slow start, I liked it. / **Although** it starts slowly, I liked it. (despite + isim, although + cümle)
- ❌ It tells the story of girl who her father keeps a lighthouse. ✅ It tells the story of **a** girl **whose** father keeps a lighthouse. (artikel ve whose; zamiri tekrar etme)

exercises.passage:
Two views on Son Ağ (The Last Net)

Mia, City Weekly: three stars
Son Ağ tells the story of Yusuf, an old fisherman who hasn't spoken to his son for forty years. The film looks wonderful. The Black Sea, which is almost a character itself, has never been filmed so beautifully. However, the plot moves so slowly that I checked my watch twice. My biggest problem is the ending. After four decades of silence, father and son make up in a single scene. Although the actors do their best, I simply didn't believe it. Despite its beauty, this is a film that I admired more than I enjoyed.

Can Aydın, film blogger: five stars
I had read several cautious reviews before I went, so I wasn't expecting much. I was wrong. Son Ağ is the most moving Turkish film I've seen this year. Yes, it's slow, but the slowness is the point: we feel the weight of every year that Yusuf has lost. Mehmet Arı, who plays Yusuf, hardly speaks, yet his face tells us everything. Some critics say the ending is too sudden. I disagree. The silence had lasted forty years because both men were proud, and pride can disappear in a moment. If you're looking for action, choose another film. If you want a story that stays with you, don't miss this one.

nodes.description: Elif'in kafesindeki ilk kitap kulübünde bir roman tartışılıyor

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Welcome to the first book club at the café! I'm so glad you've all come.
steps.translation: Kafedeki ilk kitap kulübüne hoş geldiniz! Hepinizin gelmesine çok sevindim.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Thanks for the cake, Elif. So, who wants to start with The Blue Door?
steps.translation: Pasta için teşekkürler Elif. Peki, The Blue Door ile kim başlamak ister?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I will. I'd never read a novel that was set in a lighthouse before.
steps.translation: Ben başlayayım. Daha önce bir deniz fenerinde geçen bir roman hiç okumamıştım.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: The writer, who grew up in Sinop, describes the sea so well that I could almost smell it.
steps.translation: Sinop'ta büyüyen yazar denizi o kadar iyi anlatıyor ki neredeyse kokusunu alabildim.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: I agree. But I found the first hundred pages quite boring, to be honest.
steps.translation: Katılıyorum. Ama açıkçası ilk yüz sayfayı epey sıkıcı buldum.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Really? I thought the beginning was the best part. Nothing happens, but you feel the tension.
steps.translation: Gerçekten mi? Bence başlangıç en iyi kısımdı. Hiçbir şey olmuyor ama gerilimi hissediyorsun.

steps.prompt: Elif kitabın başlangıcı hakkında ne düşünüyor?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Maybe. I had almost given up when the letters appeared. After that, I couldn't put it down.
steps.translation: Olabilir. Mektuplar ortaya çıktığında neredeyse bırakmıştım. Ondan sonra elimden bırakamadım.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: The letters were brilliant. The daughter finds them in a box that her mother had hidden.
steps.translation: Mektuplar harikaydı. Kız onları annesinin sakladığı bir kutuda buluyor.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: And they change everything, don't they? Suddenly we understand why the father never left the island.
steps.translation: Ve her şeyi değiştiriyorlar, değil mi? Birden babanın adadan neden hiç ayrılmadığını anlıyoruz.

steps.prompt: Sam'in "And they change everything" cümlesindeki "they" neyi anlatıyor?

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: What did you think of the ending? I wish the writer had explained more.
steps.translation: Sonu hakkında ne düşündünüz? Keşke yazar daha fazla açıklasaydı.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I liked it. Although it's open, it gives readers the freedom to decide for themselves.
steps.translation: Ben beğendim. Açık uçlu olsa da okura kendi kararını verme özgürlüğü tanıyor.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: I'm with Deniz. If everything is explained, a story is so easy to forget.
steps.translation: Deniz'e katılıyorum. Her şey açıklanırsa bir hikâyeyi unutmak çok kolay oluyor.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Fair enough. So, out of five stars, what would you give it?
steps.translation: Haklısınız. Peki, beş yıldız üzerinden kaç verirdiniz?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Four. I'd take one star away because of the slow start.
steps.translation: Dört. Yavaş başlangıç yüzünden bir yıldız kırardım.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Five for me. It's the kind of book you want to read again straight away.
steps.translation: Benden beş. Hemen yeniden okumak isteyeceğin türden bir kitap.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: I'll say three and a half. The writing is beautiful, but the plot didn't grab me until page one hundred.
steps.translation: Ben üç buçuk diyeceğim. Dili çok güzel ama olay örgüsü yüzüncü sayfaya kadar beni sarmadı.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Then you have to read it again, Elif. It's always better the second time.
steps.translation: O zaman tekrar okumalısın Elif. İkinci seferde hep daha iyi oluyor.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Maybe after I open the second café! Right, next month it's my choice. Any ideas?
steps.translation: Belki ikinci kafeyi açtıktan sonra! Tamam, gelecek ay seçim benim. Fikri olan var mı?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Something shorter, please. I read this one on the ferry, and it took me three weeks.
steps.translation: Daha kısa bir şey lütfen. Bunu vapurda okudum ve üç haftamı aldı.

units.title: Bence… çünkü…
units.description: Forumda görüş bildirmek, gerekçe vermek ve karşı görüşe kibarca yanıt vermek
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Bir forum zincirinde kimin hangi görüşü savunduğunu ve neden savunduğunu bulabilirsin.
- Bir tartışmada görüşünü iki gerekçeyle söyleyebilirsin.
- Karşı görüşü kabul edip kibarca yanıt verebilirsin (I see your point. However…).
- Bir foruma 100 kelimelik düzenli bir yanıt yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- Forum okurken her kullanıcının adının yanına tek kelimelik bir not al: lehte, aleyhte, ortada.
- Fikir değişimini gösteren sözcükleri yakala: *I see both sides*, *fair enough*, *I suppose*, *I'm not convinced*.
- Gölgeleme (shadow) ile kibar katılmama kalıplarını ezberle; tonunu da taklit et, çünkü kibarlık tonda da duyulur.
- Hikâyeyi önce metinsiz dinle ve her konuşmacının fikrini tek cümleyle yaz. Sonra metni açıp kontrol et.
- Konuşma turunu dört adımda kur: görüş, gerekçe, karşı görüş, cevap.

## Model metin
> Thanks for starting this thread, Elif. In my opinion, a weekend rule is a good idea, but a complete ban would be a mistake. First of all, many students and freelancers have nowhere quiet to work. A café that welcomes them will have loyal customers. Secondly, people who work on laptops usually come on weekdays, when cafés are quiet anyway.
>
> KeremCodes says that a ban sends the wrong message. I see his point. However, families also need a place where they can relax at weekends. If both groups have their own time, everyone wins. Why not try it for a month?

Yapı: 1. paragraf görüşü söyler ve iki gerekçe verir (*First of all*, *Secondly*). 2. paragraf karşı görüşü anar, kabul eder ve yanıtlar (*I see his point. However…*), sonra bir öneriyle biter.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ I am agree with you. ✅ I agree **with** you. (agree bir fiil; be gerekmez. Edat **with**, to değil.)
- ❌ The cafés are important for the students. ✅ Cafés are important for students. (Genel anlamda konuşurken **the** kullanma.)

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Deniz, I'm writing an article about working from home. Can I ask you a few questions?
steps.translation: Deniz, evden çalışma üzerine bir makale yazıyorum. Sana birkaç soru sorabilir miyim?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Sure. Actually, it's a hot topic at work. Our boss wants everyone back in the office.
steps.translation: Tabii. Aslında bu, iş yerinde çok tartışılan bir konu. Patronumuz herkesi ofise geri istiyor.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Five days a week? How do people feel about that?
steps.translation: Haftada beş gün mü? İnsanlar bu konuda ne hissediyor?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Most of the team are against it. Before the start-up grew, we had always worked from home on Fridays.
steps.translation: Ekibin çoğu buna karşı. Şirket büyümeden önce cumaları hep evden çalışırdık.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: I think your boss is right, to be honest. I miss talking to people face to face.
steps.translation: Açıkçası bence patronun haklı. İnsanlarla yüz yüze konuşmayı özlüyorum.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Really, Kerem? You're the one who told me you'd never go back to an office!
steps.translation: Gerçekten mi Kerem? Bir daha asla ofise dönmeyeceğini bana söyleyen sendin!

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: I know, but I've changed my mind. At home, I sometimes don't speak to anyone all day.
steps.translation: Biliyorum ama fikrimi değiştirdim. Evde bazen bütün gün kimseyle konuşmuyorum.

steps.prompt: Kerem'in evden çalışma hakkındaki görüşü nasıl değişti?

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: That's a fair point. Loneliness is a real problem for people who work alone.
steps.translation: Haklı bir nokta. Yalnızlık, tek başına çalışan insanlar için gerçek bir sorun.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Maybe, but our office is an hour and a half from my flat. That's three hours on the road every day.
steps.translation: Olabilir ama ofisimiz evime bir buçuk saat uzaklıkta. Bu her gün üç saat yol demek.

steps.prompt: Deniz'in evi ile ofis arası tek yön ne kadar sürüyor?

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: So what would you suggest?
steps.translation: Peki sen ne önerirsin?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Three days in the office and two at home. Meetings on office days, quiet work at home.
steps.translation: Üç gün ofiste, iki gün evde. Toplantılar ofis günlerinde, sessiz işler evde.

choices: Haftada üç gün ofis, iki gün ev
steps.answer: Haftada üç gün ofis, iki gün ev

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: That sounds sensible. Although I like the office, I wouldn't want to commute that far.
steps.translation: Mantıklı görünüyor. Ofisi sevsem de o kadar uzağa gidip gelmek istemezdim.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Has anyone suggested this to your boss?
steps.translation: Bunu patronuna öneren oldu mu?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Not yet. Everyone complains in the kitchen, but nobody says anything in meetings.
steps.translation: Henüz değil. Herkes mutfakta şikâyet ediyor ama toplantılarda kimse bir şey söylemiyor.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Then you should write it down. A clear proposal with reasons is hard to ignore.
steps.translation: O zaman bunu yazıya dökmelisin. Gerekçeli, net bir öneriyi görmezden gelmek zordur.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: And include numbers. How many hours does the team spend commuting each week?
steps.translation: Bir de rakam ekle. Ekip her hafta yolda kaç saat geçiriyor?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Good idea. I'll collect them on Monday and send the proposal by Friday.
steps.translation: İyi fikir. Pazartesi bunları toplarım ve öneriyi cumaya kadar gönderirim.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Perfect. Can I quote you in my article? I won't use your real name.
steps.translation: Harika. Makalemde senden alıntı yapabilir miyim? Gerçek adını kullanmayacağım.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Only if you send it to me before it's published!
steps.translation: Ancak yayımlanmadan önce bana gönderirsen!

Thanks for starting this thread, Elif. In my opinion, a weekend rule is a good idea, but a complete ban would be a mistake. First of all, many students and freelancers have nowhere quiet to work. units.title: Dönüm noktası
units.description: Hayatındaki bir dönüm noktasını anlatmak, sunmak ve blog yazısına dökmek
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Hayatından bir dönüm noktasını iki dakikalık bir konuşmayla sunabilirsin.
- Bir blog yazısında olayların sırasını, yazarın duygularını ve pişmanlıklarını anlayabilirsin.
- Birinin dönüm noktası hikâyesini dinleyip ana fikri ve ayrıntıları yakalayabilirsin.
- Dönüm noktanı anlatan 150 kelimelik bir blog yazısı yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- **4/3/2 tekniği:** Sunumunu önce 4 dakikada, sonra aynı içeriği 3 dakikada, en son 2 dakikada anlat. Her turda daha akıcı ve daha kısa olursun.
- Sunumu üç parçaya böl: önce (*Three years ago, I had just…*), o an (*Then…*), bugün (*Looking back, I wish…*).
- Gölgeleme (shadow) ile *I'd*, *had* gibi kısalmış biçimleri çalış; hızlı konuşmada *I had* çoğu zaman *I'd* olur.
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle: kim, ne zaman, ne değişti? Sonra metni aç ve past perfect cümlelerini bul.
- Blogda bir başlıkla başla, sonra aynı üç parçalı yapıyı paragraflara dök.

## Model metin
> The day I missed my flight
>
> Four years ago, I was working as an accountant in Ankara. I had planned a holiday in Spain for months, but on the day of the flight, the traffic was so bad that I missed the plane. I was furious. I sat in the airport café, where I started talking to a woman who ran a small travel company.
>
> She told me that she needed someone who could manage her accounts and speak English. Although the salary was lower, I said yes a month later. It was the most frightening decision I had ever made.
>
> Today I organise tours all over Turkey, and I love my job. Sometimes I wish I had changed careers earlier. However, I don't regret my old job, because it taught me how to work hard. Missing that flight was the luckiest thing that has ever happened to me.

Yapı: Başlık merak uyandırır. 1. paragraf önceki durumu ve olayı anlatır (*had planned*, *so … that*). 2. paragraf kararı anlatır (*although*, *the most … I had ever made*). 3. paragraf bugünü ve duyguları anlatır (*I wish I had…*, *However*).

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ I wish I changed my job earlier. ✅ I wish I **had changed** my job earlier. (Geçmişle ilgili pişmanlıkta **wish + had + V3**.)
- ❌ It was the most frightening decision I have ever made. ✅ It was the most frightening decision I **had** ever made. (Geçmişte anlatırken o ana kadar olanı **had** ile söyle.)

## Beceri testi
Bölüm 6 beceri testi 20 sorudur; geçmek için %80 doğru yap. Bölüm, bu test **ve** bu ünitenin yazma görevi (s6u15l4, blog yazısı) bittiğinde tamamlanmış sayılır.

| Bölüm | Soru | Ölçtüğü hedef |
|---|---|---|
| Dinleme | 6 | Past perfect ile anlatı (s6u1, s6u15); ilgi cümleleri (s6u3); wish (s6u6); question tags (s6u8); so … that (s6u5); although (s6u11) |
| Okuma | 8 | Bir oyun yorumunda yazarın görüşü ve gerekçesi (s6u13); dönüm noktası blogu ve yoruma yanıt (s6u15, s6u14) |
| Yazma | 4 | Past perfect ile gerekçe (s6u13); despite ile görüş (s6u13); gerekçeli görüş (s6u14); ilgi cümlesiyle dönüm noktası (s6u15) |
| Dil | 2 | Question tags (s6u8); although ile katılıp ekleme (s6u11, s6u14) |

by Ayşe

People often ask me how I became a baker. The honest answer is: by accident.

Ten years ago, I was teaching history at a high school in Bursa. I loved my students, but I had started to feel that every year was the same. One evening, the company that was making the cakes for our school's charity day cancelled at the last minute. Two hundred cakes were needed by the morning, and I had only ever baked for my family.

I stayed up all night. By the time the sun came up, I had made every single cake. I was exhausted, but I hadn't felt so excited for years. That night was my turning point.

For the next two years, I taught during the week and took baking classes at weekends. It wasn't easy. Although my friends thought I was crazy, my parents supported me. Two banks turned down my loan application, which was painful. The third one, however, said yes.

Do I wish I had started earlier? Sometimes. But I don't regret my years as a teacher. They taught me patience and how to explain things simply, which helps me every day in my baking classes.

If you're thinking about a big change, my advice is simple: you don't need to know everything at the start. You just need to start.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to our first story night! Tonight's theme is turning points.
steps.translation: Herkese iyi akşamlar, ilk hikâye gecemize hoş geldiniz! Bu akşamın teması dönüm noktaları.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Our first storyteller is someone you all know. Sam, the stage is yours.
steps.translation: İlk anlatıcımızı hepiniz tanıyorsunuz. Sam, sahne senin.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Thanks, Elif. Five years ago, I had just finished university, and I was working in an office in London.
steps.translation: Teşekkürler Elif. Beş yıl önce üniversiteyi yeni bitirmiştim ve Londra'da bir ofiste çalışıyordum.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: I had studied economics because my dad thought it was a safe choice. I was miserable.
steps.translation: Ekonomi okumuştum, çünkü babam bunun güvenli bir seçim olduğunu düşünüyordu. Çok mutsuzdum.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Then, one rainy Monday, my manager told me that my job no longer existed.
steps.translation: Sonra yağmurlu bir pazartesi müdürüm işimin artık olmadığını söyledi.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Oh no! What did you do?
steps.translation: Eyvah! Ne yaptın?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: I went home, sat on the floor and cried. Then I booked a cheap flight to Istanbul.
steps.translation: Eve gittim, yere oturdum ve ağladım. Sonra İstanbul'a ucuz bir uçak bileti aldım.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: A friend who lived in Kadıköy had invited me many times, but I'd always been too busy.
steps.translation: Kadıköy'de yaşayan bir arkadaşım beni defalarca davet etmişti ama hep çok meşguldüm.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: On my third day, I got lost and asked an old man for directions.
steps.translation: Üçüncü günümde kayboldum ve yaşlı bir adama yol sordum.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: His English was terrible, and my Turkish didn't exist, but we talked for two hours over tea.
steps.translation: Onun İngilizcesi berbattı, benim Türkçem ise yoktu ama çay içerek iki saat konuştuk.

steps.prompt: Sam yaşlı adamla ne kadar konuştu?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: He told me he had always wanted to learn English but had never found a teacher.
steps.translation: Bana hep İngilizce öğrenmek istediğini ama hiç öğretmen bulamadığını söyledi.

steps.prompt: "He told me he had always wanted to learn English" cümlesindeki "He" kim?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: That was the moment. I thought: I could be that teacher.
steps.translation: İşte o an. Şöyle düşündüm: O öğretmen ben olabilirim.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: So did you stay in Istanbul after that?
steps.translation: Peki ondan sonra İstanbul'da kaldın mı?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Not immediately. I went back to London and did a teaching course for four months.
steps.translation: Hemen değil. Londra'ya döndüm ve dört ay öğretmenlik kursuna gittim.

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Although my dad was worried, he came to my graduation and was surprisingly proud.
steps.translation: Babam endişeli olsa da mezuniyetime geldi ve şaşırtıcı derecede gururluydu.

steps.prompt: Sam'in babası sonunda Sam'in kararına nasıl baktı?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: That was four years ago, and I'm still here, and I still drink too much tea.
steps.translation: Bu dört yıl önceydi; hâlâ buradayım ve hâlâ çok fazla çay içiyorum.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Do you ever wish you'd stayed in London?
steps.translation: Hiç Londra'da kalmış olmayı dilediğin oluyor mu?

steps.speaker: Sam
steps.text: Honestly? Only when I see the rent prices there. Otherwise, never.
steps.translation: Dürüst olmak gerekirse mi? Yalnızca oradaki kiraları görünce. Onun dışında asla.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Thank you, Sam! That's such a lovely story that I nearly cried too.
steps.translation: Teşekkürler Sam! O kadar güzel bir hikâye ki neredeyse ben de ağlıyordum.

steps.speaker: Elif
steps.text: Who's next? Deniz, you promised me a story about a broken bicycle!
steps.translation: Sırada kim var? Deniz, bana bozuk bir bisiklet hikâyesi sözü vermiştin!

The day I missed my flight

Four years ago, I was working as an accountant in Ankara. I had planned a holiday in Spain for months, but on the day of the flight, the traffic was so bad that I missed the plane. I was furious. I sat in the airport café, where I started talking to a woman who ran a small travel company.

She told me that she needed someone who could manage her accounts and speak English. Although the salary was lower, I said yes a month later. It was the most frightening decision I had ever made.

Today I organise tours all over Turkey, and I love my job. Sometimes I wish I had changed careers earlier. However, I don't regret my old job, because it taught me how to work hard. Missing that flight was the luckiest thing that has ever happened to me.

Theatre review: The Night Visitor

This month, the small Moda Stage is showing The Night Visitor, a play that was first written for radio in the 1980s. It has only two actors: a lighthouse keeper and a young woman who arrives during a storm.

For the first half an hour, I was not sure about it. The set is very simple, and very little happens. However, the dialogue is so sharp that you soon forget there is no action. Zeynep Ak, who plays the young woman, is outstanding. She can make the audience laugh and, a moment later, cry.

My only real complaint is the length. At two and a half hours without a break, the play is far too long, and several people around me were checking their phones. Twenty minutes less would make it a much stronger show.

Despite this, I left the theatre with a smile. If you enjoy clever, quiet stories, buy a ticket before the end of the month. If you need car chases, stay at home.

exercises.passage:
Why I said no to a promotion
by Deniz

Last spring, my manager offered me a promotion. It came with a bigger salary, a new title and a lot more travel. Everyone expected me to say yes. I had worked hard for three years, and this was the reward.

I said no. It was the hardest decision I had ever made, and my colleagues thought I had lost my mind. But the new job would mean three nights a week in hotels, and I had just started volunteering at an animal shelter on weekday evenings. That work, which pays nothing, makes me happier than any title.

Do I wish I had more money? Of course. But I don't wish I had taken the job.

Reply from Deniz: Fair point, Taylan. However, weekends are when I see my family. For now, I'm happy with my choice.

exercises.passage:
Why I said no to a promotion
by Deniz

Last spring, my manager offered me a promotion. It came with a bigger salary, a new title and a lot more travel. Everyone expected me to say yes. I had worked hard for three years, and this was the reward.

I said no. It was the hardest decision I had ever made, and my colleagues thought I had lost my mind. But the new job would mean three nights a week in hotels, and I had just started volunteering at an animal shelter on weekday evenings. That work, which pays nothing, makes me happier than any title.

Do I wish I had more money? Of course. But I don't wish I had taken the job.
